subject: Deployment choice & PoC plan for Luma Health — next steps
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morton <alex.morton@lumahq.com>, Devon Tao <devon.tao@lumahq.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Deployment choice & PoC plan for Luma Health — next steps

Hi Alex / Devon — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a proposed PoC approach so we can align on the deployment mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC) and owners.

Summary of requirements from the call:
- Data sensitivity: primary workloads will touch PHI for appointment reminders and short clinical summaries; Luma indicated CHS-level controls required.
- Performance: expected burst to 120 requests/min with typical request sizes ~400 tokens; target p50 latency ~<350ms for 512-token gen.
- Integration: real-time webhook + streaming responses into your messaging queue; must support function calls to extract structured slots.
- Compliance: audit logs, retention controls, and KMS-backed key management are mandatory.

Options and recommendation:
- Hosted API: fastest to get started but will require strong contractual/data controls for PHI — usually fine for non-PHI or de-identified data.
- Dedicated: reserved GPUs and isolated pools; predictable throughput and easier to demonstrate latency SLOs during a short PoC.
- Private VPC (customer-managed): full network isolation and KMS/HSM options — recommended for regulated PHI workloads but longer provisioning and procurement lead time.

My recommendation for the PoC: run a 2-week Dedicated trial first to validate latency, throughput, and integration (streaming + function calling). If Dedicated meets all compliance gating items (encryption, audit logs) we can then scope a Private VPC cutover in parallel with procurement. This reduces risk and shows measurable economics before a longer Private deployment.

Proposed PoC success criteria (please confirm / edit):
1) Latency: p50 < 350ms for 512-token generation under typical load profile.
2) Throughput: sustain 120 r/min with 95th pctile latency below 700ms.
3) Feature parity: streaming + function-calling + prefix caching work end-to-end in your integration.
4) Security: KMS-managed keys, access audit logs available, and SOC2 evidence provided.
5) Cost guardrail: target token cost <= $0.XX per 1k tokens (we'll estimate based on config).

Timeline (tentative):
- Week 0 (this week): agree success criteria, identify stakeholders, share PoC checklist (attached).
- Week 1: Dedicated environment provision + integration kickoff.
- Week 2: Load/latency run + review + decision on Private VPC next steps.

Requested owners / stakeholders from Luma: engineering lead for integration, security/compliance contact for audit & KMS review, and procurement for contract/timeline. Please reply with names and availability.

Attaching: lumahq-poc-checklist.pdf (high-level tasks & required artifacts).

If that plan sounds reasonable I'll schedule a 30-min kickoff for Thursday to assign owners and lock the start date.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: lumahq-poc-checklist.pdf (stub).

From: Alex Morton <alex.morton@lumahq.com>

Date: 2027-04-18T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment choice & PoC plan for Luma Health — next steps

Thanks Aisha — appreciate the clear recap. Quick notes from our side: we are pretty strict about PHI; our compliance team will prefer a Private VPC in steady state. That said, we like the idea of a Dedicated trial as a fast way to validate integration and perf before committing to longer provisioning of VPC.

A few clarifications / asks:
- Auditability: can Dedicated provide an exportable audit trail (request logs + user actions) that our compliance team can review?
- Data flow: during Dedicated PoC, will any raw PHI be stored on Redwood-managed storage? If so, how is it encrypted and for how long?
- KMS: we need to understand KMS integration options (customer-managed keys preferred).

Stakeholders from Luma:
- Devon Tao — Engineering (cc'd) — will lead integration.
- Maya Patel — Security (I'll loop her in once we have PoC details).
- Procurement: procurement@lumahq.com (I'll loop them in for timeline/POC consent).

Agree to the 2-week Dedicated trial in principle. Please send the PoC checklist and a proposed kickoff time. Also, can you include expected GPU profile (e.g., A100/RTX6000 equivalent) and baseline latency estimates?

Thanks,
Alex Morton
Director of Product
Luma Health

Subject: Re: Deployment choice & PoC plan for Luma Health — next steps

Alex — quick technical follow-up from our infra side. Happy to own provisioning for the Dedicated trial. A few items so we scope the right config: 

- Typical Dedicated config we recommend for this profile: 2x A10G (or A100 equivalent) with autoscale headroom for short bursts. We can start with a 1-node minimum and allow burst to 3 nodes during peak tests.
- Networking: inbound webhook + outbound streaming supported over TLS. We'll provide sampling-level request logs and full audit logs for admin actions.
- KMS: Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS via our Cloud KMS integrations; for Private VPC we can add HSM-backed key options.
- Caching: we can enable prefix/KV caching to lower token spend for repeated prompts; we'll show telemetry in the console.

I'll attach a short PoC checklist (lumahq-poc-checklist.pdf) with environment variables and sample load script. For the latency estimate, under a 1–2 node Dedicated config we expect p50 ~250–400ms for 512 tokens (depends on model and quantization). We'll run a baseline with the model you choose on day 2 of the trial.

Next steps from our side:
1) Aisha to schedule kickoff (30 min).
2) Luma to confirm stakeholders and any gating compliance docs.
3) We provision Dedicated trial; Luma runs integration and load tests; we share telemetry and a short readout.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Procurement & compliance inputs for Dedicated -> Private VPC flow

Hi Alex / procurement team — looping in procurement early so we can align timelines if Luma decides to migrate from Dedicated -> Private VPC. A few procurement/legal items that often affect lead time: 

- SOC 2 / security pack: we have an up-to-date SOC 2 Type II report and a security pack (link available). Please let us know if you need a redacted copy.
- Data residency & retention: we'll provide options for retention windows and the ability to disable persistent storage in the Dedicated trial; for Private VPC we can follow your retention policy directly.
- Contracting: typical enterprise SOW + MSA; if you need a specific DPA/BAA for PHI we can provision those terms and provide a standard BAA template.

If you can share a target procurement decision date we can provide a parallel timeline for VPC provisioning. For example, if procurement needs 30 days, we can run the Dedicated PoC now and queue VPC provisioning so it completes within your timeline.

I'll also need a point of contact on the security side (name + email) to share SOC2 and KMS implementation docs.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
